problem: Concurrent agents can trigger overlapping GitHub, Netlify and Supabase work. Agents then idle on queued/running jobs, newer main revisions appear, and the original delivery loops re-enter waiting or recovery instead of progressing.
root_cause: Remote workflow state was treated as a conversational wait point instead of durable asynchronous execution state.
Production source snapshots used non-cancelling global concurrency, allowing stale reversible runs to queue behind newer main.
Some required jobs had no explicit job timeout.
PR metadata errors could fail admission after expensive external preview work had already started.
Required test coupled exact Netlify production-build parity to full_shared_suite, so control-plane-only changes still spent time rebuilding the entire site.
fix: Make remote waiting non-blocking for every chat/agent and require a resumable checkpoint.
Supersede stale reversible Production Source Snapshot runs with cancel-in-progress.
Bound production snapshot and Required test jobs to 20 minutes.
Require one active required workflow per exact candidate head and automatic resume after interruption.
Gate exact Netlify production-build parity on actual Netlify-hosted runtime/build paths rather than generic shared-suite classification.
prevention: Never use pending/queued/in_progress as a terminal user-facing state.
Do not redispatch a required run when the exact head already has one active.
Batch repository writes before CI to reduce fan-out.
Prefer latest-authoritative-main supersession for reversible production waiting work.
Control-plane-only policy/skill/workflow changes must not run full Netlify build parity unless a deploy-relevant path changed.
